brief_summary: Strip of four cards, one per low-profile switch family (Kailh Choc v1, Kailh Choc v2, Cherry MX Low Profile, Logitech GL), each annotated with a stem-shape icon, hot-swap status, relative keycap catalog size, and example boards. Makes literal the claim that 'low-profile' names a category with three-plus incompatible stem shapes rather than one spec.
data_sources: low-profile-keyboards-buying-guide.mdx § 'Two ecosystems, not one' — 'Choc v1 uses a proprietary two-prong stem... Choc v2 moved to an MX-style cross stem with a shorter skirt... v1 and v2 switches are not interchangeable with each other'; 'Cherry's own low-profile switches need low-profile keycaps specifically'; 'Logitech... GL switches started as a tweaked, proprietary version of Choc v1 on the original G915, then moved to an MX-style cross stem on newer boards like the G515'
ZSA, Voyager FAQ (https://www.zsa.io/voyager/faq/what-keyswitches-work-with-the-change-it-yourself-feature) — Voyager ships hot-swappable Kailh Choc v1 switches
Keeb.io, 'Kailh Choc V2 Switch Comparison' (https://blog.keeb.io/kailh-choc-v2-switch-comparison/) — v1/v2 stem and interchangeability differences

Tom's Hardware, Cherry MX Low Profile RGB announcement (https://www.tomshardware.com/news/cherry-mx-low-profile-rgb-mechanical-keyboard-switches,36328.html) — low-profile keycaps required for Cherry MX LP
Tom's Hardware, Logitech G515 Lightspeed TKL review (https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/gaming-keyboards/logitech-g515-lightspeed-tkl-review) — GL switch stem change from G915 to G515
